_comment_about_this_file: Splunk Enterprise/Cloud Dashboard Studio definition for the spinel-ebpf L2-L8 cross-layer view. This is an SPL dashboard assuming ingest through OTLP -> OpenTelemetry Collector -> splunk_hec exporter -> a Splunk index. The JSON is valid under python json.load. SPL field names depend on the quirks of HEC ingest, so see the README and each panel's description.
_comment_field_naming: OTLP attributes contain dots (http.route, net.tcp.state_changes and so on). In Splunk they are referenced in single quotes: 'http.route'. The real index and sourcetype depend on your environment; index=otel and sourcetype=otel:span are used here as an example. duration is the span's execution-time field, which some Collector and exporter combinations name span_duration or similar.
title: spinel-ebpf L2-L8 xlayer correlation (SPL)
description: L3/L4, L7 and L8 sit together in one span, so tenant, route, status and TCP state can be displayed across layers with no join

options.query: index=otel sourcetype=otel:span 'tenant'="$tenant$" 'http.route'="$route$" | timechart perc95(duration) AS p95 by 'http.route'

index=otel sourcetype=otel:span 'http.route'="$route$" | stats latest('net.tcp.state_changes') AS state_changes latest('net.tcp.established') AS established avg(duration) AS avg_duration count AS requests by 'tenant' 'http.route' 'http.request.method' | sort - state_changes

ds_xlayer_table.name: TCP state_changes / established table by tenant x route (L4 x L7 x L8)

options.query: | mstats sum(_value) AS count WHERE metric_name="access_class" AND index=otel_metrics BY proto tcp_state | sort - count

ds_access_class.name: Classification of a traffic burst (rate by proto x tcp_state, L3/L4)

options.query: | mstats sum(_value) AS count WHERE metric_name="access_class" AND index=otel_metrics BY action proto | sort - count

ds_access_action.name: Enforcement, pass against drop (rate by action x proto, L3/L4)

viz_latency.title: p95 latency per route (HTTP server span duration)

viz_xlayer.title: Cross-layer: tenant x route x TCP state (L4 x L7 x L8)
viz_xlayer.description: L8 (tenant) x L7 (http.route/method) x L4 (net.tcp.state_changes/established) in one table, with no join.

viz_access_class.title: Classification of a traffic burst (rate by proto x tcp_state)
viz_access_class.description: L3/L4: access_class split by 'proto' (icmp/udp/tcp/other) x 'tcp_state' (syn/established), which tells a SYN surge from established sessions at a glance. The metric index depends on your environment, for example otel_metrics.

viz_access_action.title: Enforcement, pass against drop (rate by action x proto)
viz_access_action.description: L3/L4: access_class split by 'action' (pass/drop) x 'proto', separating what XDP dropped on the spot (drop=icmp) from what it passed (pass=tcp/udp/other) -- observation and enforcement from one binary. A sudden rise in drop is a sign of an attack or a misconfiguration. The metric index depends on your environment.
